einstellungen.text: A hundred and twenty people are looking at you. And you say, "I don't know yet."
The opening. The mic echoes. The stage light is warm on your face.
Eda starts. Her half of the welcome. She's funnier than you.
Then you lead everyone through the stations. The yellow cards. The recording with Eda at the edge.
Your sheet with the word sleep. Crossed out. People laugh. In a kind way.
Your dad is standing right up front. This time, right up front.
A boy raises his hand. His question is good. And you don't know the answer.
Before, you would've just made something up. Fast. Sounding sure. As long as nobody noticed.
"I don't know yet. I'll write it down."
You pin the question to the wall. Underneath, there's room for the answer.
Then comes the applause. Not for a perfect show. For an honest one. Eda squeezes your hand.
Ms. Sen walks over with an old, yellowed index card. She pins it next to yours.
Her card is from two thousand three. Her first exhibition, back when she was a student.
It says the sentence you almost said yourself: "I'm not allowed to make mistakes."
